readers.reasoning: The scalar r in a kernels construct is treated as in a copy clause, and hf is explicitly copy. The loop reduction on r combines per-gang values with the original and stores the result. The async queue 1 is waited on before r is read, so the host sees the final value. hf is written by a single iteration, so there is no race. AND of (i+256) over i=1..64 is 256 (bit 8 common, 1&2=0). A conforming compiler must give r == 256; the wrong answer is a compiler bug.

The reduction variable r appears in a reduction clause on the enclosed loop and has no other data clause. Section 2.6.2 makes the appearance in the loop reduction an exposed access, and a scalar on a kernels construct is treated as copy. Section 2.9.11 says the combined result is stored in the original var by the end of the compute region. The async copy-out completes before the wait(1) returns. hf has an explicit copy and is written by one iteration only. The AND of (i+256) for i=1..64 is 256, so r==256 is required. Observed r differs, so compiler A is wrong.
